stem: Rosa asks an official at a police detention center whether her brother, reported as a victim of enforced disappearance, is being held there. Under RA 10353, what must the official do?
choices: Tell her to get an order from a court first
Answer only if her brother agrees to it
Refuse, since the detention records are kept secret
Immediately certify in writing whether he is there
answer: Immediately certify in writing whether he is there
hints: RA 10353 puts duties on officials so that families can find people who have disappeared. Think about what Rosa needs.
Recall Section 8 of RA 10353: the duty to certify in writing the results of an inquiry about a disappeared person.
Section 8 says how fast and in what form the official must answer. Compare each choice with that, and recall what Section 10 says about the register of detained persons.

solution.methodName: Match the situation to the provision

steps.action: Spot the situation: a relative asks a detention official about a reported victim of enforced disappearance.
Find the provision: RA 10353, Section 8. It covers inquiries by "a family member, relative, lawyer, representative of a human rights organization or a member of the media".

Section 8 says the official "shall immediately issue a certification in writing to the inquiring person or entity on the presence or absence and/or information on the whereabouts of such disappeared person".
steps.why: The written certification is a record of the answer. It must state the date and time of the inquiry and the response.

steps.action: Section 10 also says relatives "shall have free access" to the official register of persons detained, so the records are not secret from her.
The answer is: immediately certify in writing whether he is there.

trapNotes.Tell her to get an order from a court fi: Section 8 sets no court step. The official must answer the inquiry "immediately".
trapNotes.Answer only if her brother agrees to it: Section 8 does not wait for the detained person's consent. It covers inquiries by "a family member, relative, lawyer" and others.
trapNotes.Refuse, since the detention records are: Section 10 says relatives have "free access" to the register of detained persons, and its information "shall be made available to the public".

sourceRef.citation: RA 10353 (Anti-Enforced or Involuntary Disappearance Act of 2012), Sections 8 and 10
